live.name: NICKEL FOXCROFT
live.headline: NICKEL FOXCROFT: a threat actor known by many names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists NICKEL FOXCROFT under many aliases, including APT37 and ScarCruft, and names eight tools tied to it. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: NICKEL FOXCROFT is the Secureworks name for a threat actor tracked under many other names.
Its aliases include APT37, ATK4, Group 123, InkySquid, Moldy Pisces, Operation Daybreak, Operaton Erebus, RICOCHET CHOLLIMA, Reaper, ScarCruft, TA-RedAnt and Venus 121.
The catalogue links eight tools to the actor: Bluelight, Chinotto, GOLDBACKDOOR, KevDroid, KoSpy, PoorWeb, ROKRAT and final1stpy.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: NICKEL FOXCROFT
next.headline: NICKEL FOXCROFT (APT37, ScarCruft): a long-running espionage group focused on Korean targets
next.in_short: Vendors describe NICKEL FOXCROFT, also tracked as APT37 and ScarCruft, as a North Korea-aligned espionage group active since at least 2012. It targets mainly South Korea and uses cloud services, USB media and mobile spyware.

sentences.t: Secureworks tracks this actor as NICKEL FOXCROFT. Its catalogue record lists many aliases, including APT37, ScarCruft, Reaper, Group 123, InkySquid and RICOCHET CHOLLIMA.
CrowdStrike describes RICOCHET CHOLLIMA as a North Korea-nexus targeted intrusion adversary. It says the group has been involved in espionage since at least 2016.
ESET says ScarCruft, also known as APT37 or Reaper, has operated since at least 2012 and is suspected to be a North Korean espionage group.
Lookout calls ScarCruft a North Korean state-sponsored cyber espionage group active since 2012. S2W likewise describes it as a group known to be behind North Korea, active since 2012.
CrowdStrike says the group's observed operations have almost exclusively targeted the Republic of Korea. It assesses the focus to be government officials, NGOs, academics and journalists.
ESET says the group seems mainly interested in government and military organisations. It says South Korea is the main focus, but other Asian countries have also been targeted.
Kudelski Security and Sekoia describe the related cluster Reaper as focused on North Korean defectors, South Korean activists and NGOs.
Lookout says the group has also operated in countries including Japan, Vietnam, Russia, Nepal, China, India and Romania.
Zscaler says APT37 has used malicious shortcut (LNK) files as an initial vector for years.

S2W analysed a 2020 watering-hole attack. It ended in a ROKRAT variant that used legitimate cloud services such as pCloud, Yandex, Box and Dropbox for command and control. S2W judges the activity to relate to ScarCruft.

Lookout describes KoSpy, Android spyware disguised as utility apps and spread through Google Play and Firebase Firestore. It attributes KoSpy to APT37 with medium confidence and notes ties to APT43 infrastructure.
Lookout also notes that North Korean groups share infrastructure, targeting and techniques, which makes attribution to one actor harder.
Zscaler reported the Ruby Jumper campaign in February 2026. It spreads over removable media to reach air-gapped networks and delivers tools including RESTLEAF, SNAKEDROPPER, THUMBSBD and BLUELIGHT.
Zscaler says that, to its knowledge, this was the first time APT37 abused Zoho WorkDrive.

ESET reports a supply-chain attack by ScarCruft on a video game platform for the Yanbian region of China. It was probably under way since late 2024 and delivered the Android BirdCall backdoor through trojanized games.
ESET infers the main targets are ethnic Koreans in Yanbian, most likely refugees or defectors. It says the backdoor collects files, contacts, SMS, screenshots and voice recordings.
People who work on Korea-related issues, and groups that help defectors, should treat unexpected shortcut files, USB drives and unofficial app or game downloads with caution.
